q: Which amendment added the word "Secular" to the Preamble?
x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Socialist, Secular and Integrity. It is the only time the Preamble was changed.

q: Who called the Preamble the "keynote of the Constitution"?
x: Ernest Barker: keynote. Munshi: political horoscope. Palkhivala: identity card. Bhargava: soul.

q: K.M. Munshi described the Preamble as the…
o: Heart and soul of the Constitution
x: Munshi: political horoscope. "Heart and soul" was Ambedkar's phrase for Article 32.

q: Who called the Preamble the "soul of the Constitution"?
x: Thakurdas Bhargava called it the soul of the Constitution.

q: In which case did the Supreme Court say the Preamble IS part of the Constitution?
x: Berubari (1960) said no; Kesavananda Bharati (1973) said yes. It can be amended but not enforced in court.

q: Which statement about the Preamble is correct today?
o: It can be amended but cannot be enforced in a court
It can be enforced in a court
It is not part of the Constitution
x: Since Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Preamble is part of the Constitution, can be amended (without hurting the basic structure), and is not enforceable.

q: When did the Constituent Assembly first meet?
x: 9 December 1946, with Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary chairman. On 13 December Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution.

q: Who was the temporary chairman of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary chairman; Dr Rajendra Prasad was then elected permanent President.

q: Who was the constitutional adviser to the Constituent Assembly?
x: Sir B.N. Rau was the constitutional adviser. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

q: The Objectives Resolution, which later became the Preamble, was moved by…
x: Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946.

q: The Constitution was adopted on…
x: Adopted 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day); in force 26 January 1950.

q: Why was 26 January chosen for the Constitution to come into force?
o: Congress had celebrated Purna Swaraj Day on 26 January 1930
The Cabinet Mission arrived that day
The Drafting Committee was formed that day
x: The Congress observed 26 January 1930 as Purna Swaraj (complete independence) Day.

q: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to make the Constitution?
x: From 9 December 1946 to 26 November 1949: 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

q: The Constituent Assembly was set up under which plan?
x: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.

q: Which pair of Schedule and subject is WRONG?
x: Oaths are in the 3rd Schedule. The 2nd Schedule has salaries. Memory: 2 = Salary, 3 = Swearing, 4 = Seats.

q: Which Schedule lists the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states?
x: 4th Schedule = Seats in the Rajya Sabha.

q: How many languages are in the Eighth Schedule?
x: 22 languages, Odia among them.

q: The Ninth Schedule, which protects certain laws from court review, was added by…
x: The 1st Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule, mainly for land reform laws.

q: How many subjects are given to panchayats in the 11th Schedule?
x: 11th Schedule: 29 subjects for panchayats (73rd Amendment). 12th Schedule: 18 for municipalities (74th).

q: Scheduled Areas in Odisha are covered by which Schedule?
x: The 5th Schedule covers Scheduled Areas in states like Odisha. The 6th is only for Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

q: The right to freedom of religion is in which Articles?
x: Religion: 25–28. Freedom: 19–22. Culture and education: 29–30. Against exploitation: 23–24.

q: Which Article abolished untouchability?
x: Article 17 ends untouchability. Article 18 ends titles.

q: Article 21A gives the right to…
o: Free education for children aged 6 to 14
x: Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment (2002).

q: Which amendment removed the right to property from Fundamental Rights?
x: The 44th Amendment removed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31. Property is now a legal right under Article 300A.

q: The right to property is now a legal right under which Article?
x: Article 300A: no one can be deprived of property except by law.

q: In the Puttaswamy case (2017), the Supreme Court held that…
x: Nine judges led by CJI J.S. Khehar held privacy to be part of Article 21. It is not absolute.

q: In 2025 the Supreme Court said maternity leave is part of which Article?
x: It called maternity leave part of reproductive rights under Article 21, even for a third child.

q: The right to vote comes from which Article?
x: Article 326 (adult suffrage) and election law. Voting is not a Fundamental Right.

q: Which writ orders a public officer to do his duty?
x: Mandamus = "we command".

q: Which writ asks a person "by what authority" he holds a public post?
x: Quo warranto questions the right to hold a public office.

q: Which writ is used to bring a detained person before the court?
x: Habeas corpus = "produce the body".

q: A higher court cancels an order already passed by a lower court through which writ?
x: Certiorari cancels an order already passed. Prohibition stops a case while it is still going on.

q: Article 35A, which ended in 2019, concerned…
o: Special rights of permanent residents of Jammu and Kashmir
Rights of minorities to run schools
x: It ended when Article 370 was removed on 5 August 2019.

q: Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became Union Territories on…
x: Article 370 was removed on 5 August 2019; the two UTs came into being on 31 October 2019.

q: Which Article is called the foreign policy Article?
x: Article 51 asks the State to promote international peace and security.

q: Which Directive Principle was added in 1976?
x: The 42nd Amendment added 39A (free legal aid), 39(f), 43A and 48A.

q: Which Article asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife?
x: 48A was added in 1976. Article 51A(g) is the matching Fundamental Duty.

q: Which Article asks for separation of the judiciary from the executive?
x: Article 50, a Directive Principle.

q: The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from…
x: From the USSR. Directive Principles came from Ireland.

q: Which amendment added the 11th Fundamental Duty (sending children aged 6–14 to school)?
x: The 86th Amendment added Article 21A and the 11th duty.

q: Single citizenship was borrowed from…
x: Britain gave the parliamentary system, single citizenship, rule of law and writs.

q: Nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha was borrowed from…
x: Ireland gave Directive Principles, nominated Rajya Sabha members and the method of electing the President.

q: The Concurrent List and joint sitting of Parliament were borrowed from…
x: Australia: Concurrent List, joint sitting, free trade between states.

q: Judicial review and impeachment of the President were borrowed from…
x: USA: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independent courts, impeachment, Vice-President.

q: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency was borrowed from…
x: From the Weimar Constitution of Germany.

q: The procedure to amend the Constitution was borrowed from…
x: South Africa: amendment procedure and election of Rajya Sabha members.

q: "Procedure established by law" was borrowed from…
x: From Japan. The USA has "due process of law".

q: A strong Centre with residuary powers was borrowed from…
x: Canada: strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre, Governors appointed by the Centre.

q: Which was the biggest single source of the Indian Constitution?
x: It gave the federal set-up, the Governor's office, Public Service Commissions and emergency powers.

q: The method of electing the President is in which Article?
x: Article 55(3): proportional representation by single transferable vote, secret ballot. Article 54 names the electoral college.

q: Who does NOT vote in the election of the President?
o: Elected MPs of the Lok Sabha
Elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry
x: President: elected MPs + elected MLAs (incl. Delhi, Puducherry). Nominated members do not vote.

q: Who elects the Vice-President of India?
o: All members of both Houses of Parliament
Only elected members of both Houses
Members of the Rajya Sabha only
x: All MPs, elected and nominated. MLAs do not vote.

q: What is the minimum age to become President of India?
x: President and Vice-President: 35. Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council: 30. Lok Sabha: 25.

q: Under which Article does the President issue ordinances?
x: Article 123 for the President; Article 213 for the Governor. Article 72 is the pardoning power.

q: Under which Article does the President grant pardons?
x: Article 72 (President). Article 161 is the Governor's pardoning power.

q: Who is the present Vice-President of India?
x: Elected in September 2025 after Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned.

q: Which statement about the Prime Minister is FALSE?
o: The PM must be a member of the Lok Sabha
The PM is appointed by the President
A non-MP can become PM for six months
The Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha
x: The PM can be from either House; Indira Gandhi and Manmohan Singh were Rajya Sabha members.

q: The 91st Amendment limits the Council of Ministers to what share of the Lok Sabha?
x: 15% (2003). In states the same rule applies, with a minimum of 12 ministers.

q: The Attorney General of India is appointed under which Article?
x: Article 76. He can speak in Parliament but cannot vote. Article 165 is the Advocate General of a state.

q: How are Lok Sabha members elected?
x: The candidate with the most votes wins. STV is used for the President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha and Councils.

q: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
x: Rajya Sabha now: 233 elected + 12 nominated = 245.

q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
x: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar.

q: How many joint sittings of Parliament have been held so far?
x: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission (1978) and POTA (2002).

q: A joint sitting was held in 2002 to pass which law?
x: The Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002.

q: Money given in advance so the government can run until the full budget is passed is called…
x: Vote on Account covers about two months.

q: The Constitution calls the budget the…
x: Article 112: Annual Financial Statement.

q: If the Rajya Sabha suggests changes to a Money Bill, the Lok Sabha…
o: Must send it to the President
x: The Rajya Sabha can only recommend; the Lok Sabha decides.

q: Which is a special power of the Rajya Sabha?
o: Allowing creation of a new All India Service
x: Only the Rajya Sabha can allow a law on a State List subject (Art. 249) or a new All India Service (Art. 312), by a two-thirds vote.

q: Which Article lets Parliament make a law on a State List subject after a Rajya Sabha resolution?
x: Article 249 needs a two-thirds Rajya Sabha resolution.

q: At what age do High Court judges retire?
x: High Court: 62. Supreme Court: 65.

q: The 99th Amendment (NJAC) came into force on 13 April 2015. What happened next?
o: The Supreme Court struck it down in October 2015
x: The NJAC was struck down in October 2015, so the collegium system continues.

q: Who can create or abolish a State Legislative Council?
o: Parliament, after a resolution of the State Assembly
x: Article 169: the Assembly passes a resolution, then Parliament makes a law.

q: What is the minimum age to be a member of a State Legislative Council?
x: 30 years.

q: Delhi became the National Capital Territory by which amendment?
x: The 69th Amendment (1991).

q: Which state was the first to start Panchayati Raj?
x: Nagaur, Rajasthan, 2 October 1959, on the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's advice.

q: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) is linked to…
x: It proposed three-level Panchayati Raj: village, block, district.

q: The 74th Amendment on municipalities came into force on…
x: 73rd (panchayats): 24 April 1993. 74th (municipalities): 1 June 1993.

q: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on…
x: 24 April, when the 73rd Amendment came into force in 1993.

q: Elections to panchayats and municipalities are conducted by the…
x: The State Election Commission, not the ECI.

q: The Election Commission is under which Article?
x: Article 324. UPSC: 315; Finance Commission: 280; CAG: 148.

q: National Voters' Day is observed on…
x: 25 January, the founding day of the Election Commission (1950).

q: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by…
o: An Act of Parliament, at the request of the states
x: Article 315.

q: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
x: The CAG (Article 148) is appointed by the President for 6 years or till age 65.

q: The Finance Commission consists of…
o: The Finance Minister and state finance ministers
x: Article 280: chairman + 4 members, every five years.

q: After retiring, the UPSC Chairman can take up…
o: No further job under any government
x: Article 319: the UPSC Chairman cannot take any later government job.

q: The NHRC was set up under which law?
x: It is a statutory body, not a constitutional one.

q: Who was the first chairperson of the NHRC?
x: Justice Ranganath Mishra, from Odisha.

q: Who is NOT on the committee that selects the NHRC chairperson?
o: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: Committee: PM, Speaker, Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman, both Leaders of Opposition, Home Minister.

q: The Central Vigilance Commission was set up on the advice of the…
x: Set up in 1964; got legal status in 2003.

q: Who was India's first Lokpal?
x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, 2019, under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

q: Which amendment is called the "Mini Constitution"?
x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) made the widest changes.

q: Education was moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by…
x: Education, forests and three more subjects moved in 1976.

q: Which amendment reorganised states on language lines?
x: The 7th Amendment (1956).

q: Which amendment gave 10% reservation to the economically weaker section (EWS)?
x: 103rd (2019). The 102nd made the Backward Classes Commission constitutional.

q: Which amendment ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha?
x: The 104th also extended SC/ST seat reservation to 2030.

q: Which amendment brought in GST?
x: The 101st Amendment (2016); GST started on 1 July 2017.

q: National Emergency has been declared how many times?
The 44th Amendment replaced "internal disturbance" in Article 352 with…
x: National Emergency can now be declared for war, external aggression or armed rebellion.

q: Which of these is a STATE law, not a central law?
x: The Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act is a state law. The others were made by Parliament.

q: President's Rule in a state can last at most…
x: Article 356, renewed every six months, up to 3 years.

q: Who can put "reasonable restrictions" on the freedoms in Article 19?
x: Only the legislature, by making a law.

q: The President addresses Parliament at the first session of every year under which Article?
x: Article 87: special address after each general election and at the first session of each year.
